summary: Learners express one quantity as a fraction of another: 'a as a fraction of b' = a/b, where the quantity after 'of' is the denominator (the whole). Mastery requires (1) converting both quantities to the SAME unit before forming the fraction (45 minutes as a fraction of 2 hours is 45/120 = 3/8, not 45/2), (2) accepting results greater than one whole when the first quantity is bigger (3 hours as a fraction of 2 hours = 3/2), and (3) simplifying and interpreting the fraction back in context.
misconceptions: Writing the raw numbers without converting to a common unit (45/2 for 45 minutes as a fraction of 2 hours).
Putting the quantities the wrong way round — ignoring that the quantity after 'of' is the denominator.
Believing a fraction must be less than 1, so being unable to accept or interpret a result greater than 1 (3 hours as a fraction of 2 hours = 3/2).
Forgetting to simplify, or simplifying incorrectly, leaving the comparison obscured.

activities.title: The fraction-of bench: convert units, then form the fraction
steps: Start with two quantities in different units, e.g. 45 minutes and 2 hours, and say in words which quantity is the whole (the one after 'of' — here 2 hours).
Before writing any fraction, convert both to a common unit: split the 2-hour bar into 120 minute-segments and highlight the 45.
Form the fraction from the shaded bar: 45 out of 120, then simplify the equivalent-fraction chain 45/120 → 9/24 → 3/8.

In a second round, take 3 hours as a fraction of 2 hours: shade 3 hours against a 2-hour whole bar so the shading runs past the end of one whole and spills into a second bar; read the fraction as 3/2.
State what 3/2 means here in words: '3 hours is one and a half times the two hours' / 'more than the whole'.
Check yourself with an obvious case: 1 hour as a fraction of 2 hours should be 1/2 — confirm your method gives it.
activities.insight: Both quantities must be in the same unit before forming a fraction, the quantity after 'of' is the denominator, and the comparison fraction can exceed one whole when the first quantity is larger.

activities.title: Form, simplify and interpret — including improper results
steps: Fill in the blank: '45 min as a fraction of 2 h = ___', giving the simplified fraction (3/8) and rejecting the un-converted 45/2.
Identify which quantity is the denominator in a given 'a as a fraction of b' statement and justify why.
Tackle an item whose answer exceeds 1: write 150 cm as a fraction of 1 m in simplest form (= 3/2), avoiding 2/3 (wrong way round) and 150/1 (no conversion).
After each answer, write one sentence interpreting the fraction in the original context.
activities.insight: Forming, simplifying and interpreting the fraction — including when it is greater than 1 — is a single connected skill, with the not-converting and wrong-way-round errors as the key pitfalls.

activities.title: Annotated reference bar: 'of → denominator' and 'convert units first'
steps: Study a bar showing 45 of 120 minutes shaded; tap the word 'of' to reveal that it marks the whole/denominator.
Tap the bar to reveal the common-unit conversion (2 h = 120 min) that had to happen first.
Use this card as a quick check before forming any 'fraction-of' answer.
activities.insight: The phrase 'a as a fraction of b' always puts the quantity after 'of' as the denominator, and units must be made common before the fraction is formed.

checkQuestion: Write 45 minutes as a fraction of 2 hours, as simply as you can. Then explain how you got it.
checkAnswer: 3/8. Because 2 hours = 120 minutes, 45 minutes as a fraction of 2 hours is 45/120, which simplifies to 3/8. (Both quantities must be in the same unit — minutes — before forming the fraction.)
